chandra: heads-up: i prototyped an adaptive work-stealing layer on top of our continuous batcher. tradeoffs look promising but we need to decide if we ship this or stick with pool-ownership model. thoughts? :thinking:

alex: curious — what's the triggering signal for a steal? latency tail or queue fill?

chandra: primary signal is observed packing slack + deadline misses. i used a rolling 1s window: if tail P99 > 60ms or local batch < steal_threshold_tokens then try steal. pseudocode below:

```
// naive sketch
if (local_batch_worth < min_efficiency && neighbor.queue_len > 0) {
  request_steal(neighbor);
}
on_steal_request(amt) {
  if (can_spare(amt)) move_tokens(amt)
  else respond_fail();
}
```

lia: nice. main worry is kv-cache fragmentation + residency. if we move inflight items between GPUs we lose kvcache locality and will regen which can spike token compute. how do we handle sticky K/V? :grimacing:

chandra: agreed — i added a soft-pin: we only steal requests whose kv footprint is below a threshold or whose model segment is compatible with target device. otherwise we prefer cooperative spill (hand back to queue).

sam: what about fairness across tenants? stealing could starve small tenants if heavy tenants siphon work. we need a credit or lease system.

tj: complexity vs observability: pool-ownership is simpler to reason about and matches existing telemetry. work-stealing will need new traces (steal-events, kvcache-miss-after-steal) and we need to expose them in the console. any plan for that?

chandra: yes, i instrumented three events: steal.request, steal.grant|deny, steal.kv_regen. we can add dashboard panels and alerting. also added a counter to track bytes regen per-minute.

eva: runbook implication: what happens on partial steal failures? do we rollback, or finish on target? gotta avoid double-execution.

chandra: we do not duplicate execution. steal is only about moving the request descriptor; actual execution is single-owner. if grant fails mid-transfer we retry local execution. also added an idempotency token per request to prevent double-run.

alex: perf numbers? does it actually reduce p99 vs just better batching rules?

chandra: in sim (mixed workload, 70% long gen, 30% short) — adaptive-steal reduced global P99 by ~18% and increased GPU utilization by ~9%. but kvcache regen cost increased token-work by ~4% on average.

lia: sounds like a net win for latency-critical endpoints. but for cost-sensitive endpoints that regen hit might be unacceptable. maybe make steal policy tenant-configurable?

sam: +1. expose policy: { mode: "never", "cooperative", "aggressive" } and a tenant-level kv-sensitivity flag. default cooperative.

tj: also consider bounded stealing: only steal up to X requests per minute per-pod to limit oscillation. add hysteresis.

chandra: implemented hysteresis (cooldown 500ms per-victim) and a per-pod steal_budget refilled slowly. helps reduce ping-pong.

infra-bot: deploy-trigger: canary/steal-experiment-2026-03 started on cluster-3. link: https://internal/redwood/runs/steal-experiment-2026-03

eva: great — can we agree on test plan before canary reaches prod? i'd like fault injection: force kvcache-miss-after-steal and kill-stealer mid-handshake.

chandra: test plan: 1) small canary (5% traffic) on canary-3, 2) inject kv_miss fault to measure regen cost, 3) run tenant-isolation sims (heavy vs light), 4) verify console metrics and runbook triggers.

lia: add a togglable tenant policy and ensure default conservative config for enterprise tenants.

sam: one more thing — rollback strategy: if P50/P99 regress > 10% for any tenant during canary, auto-fallback to pool-ownership for that shard. implementable?

chandra: yes, canary controller will monitor and flip a per-shard feature flag. fallback path is cheap: stop steal requests, let ownership settle.

tj: ok from ops POV if we have the traces and rollback. please make dashboards and alert runbook doc before canary.

chandra: will do. i'll push a short RFC follow-up summarizing: steal triggers, kv heuristics, tenant policy, observability, canary plan, rollback. posting in #eng-runtime by EOD. :thumbsup:
